properties.title: Missouri Woman Suffrage Association organizes
properties.description: Virginia Minor, Rebecca Hazard, Lucretia Hall, Penelope Allen and Anna Clapp met at Mercantile Library in May 1867 to organize the Woman Suffrage Association of Missouri, building a local campaign for women’s voting rights.
properties.source: City of St. Louis Cultural Resources Office
properties.locationAccuracy: Approximate former library-hall address at 510 Locust; not the current library at UMSL or a surviving meeting room.
properties.coordinateEvidence: Official/historical source supplies 510 Locust St, Saint Louis, Missouri. Esri World Geocoding matched 510 Locust St, Saint Louis, Missouri, 63101 (score 100; PointAddress); rounded address/intersection reference, not a surveyed historic footprint.

properties.title: First World Series game played in St. Louis
properties.description: Sportsman’s Park hosted the city’s first World Series game. Cardinals pitcher Jesse Haines threw a shutout and homered as St. Louis defeated the Yankees 4–0.
properties.locationAccuracy: Commemorative marker at the former Sportsman’s Park site; the stadium is gone. This pin is not home plate.

properties.title: 1904 World’s Fair opens
properties.description: The Louisiana Purchase Exposition opened on April 30, 1904. Its extensive grounds occupied western Forest Park and adjacent land; the surviving Palace of Fine Arts is now the Saint Louis Art Museum.
properties.locationAccuracy: Art Museum commemorative marker within the former fair grounds; not an exact opening-ceremony location or the fair boundary.

properties.title: The Zebulon M. Pike brings steam navigation to St. Louis
properties.description: The steamboat Zebulon M. Pike docked at St. Louis in 1817, signaling the shift from keelboats toward steam-powered river transport. Stone wharves and warehouses subsequently transformed the commercial waterfront.
properties.locationAccuracy: Approximate central riverfront reference near the modern riverwalk. The vessel’s exact 1817 berth is not known from the cited source.
properties.locationBasis: Approximate central riverfront reference near the modern riverwalk. The vessel’s exact 1817 berth is not known from the cited source.

properties.title: Zooline Railroad begins carrying zoo visitors
properties.description: Saint Louis Zoo opened its miniature railroad, creating a new way for visitors to travel through the grounds. The railroad became a lasting part of the zoo’s public experience.
properties.locationAccuracy: Approximate zoo reference point; the railroad follows a route across the grounds rather than one location.

properties.title: Zumwalt’s Fort shelters frontier families
properties.description: Jacob Zumwalt’s log home became a refuge for local settler families during the War of 1812. Archaeology later located original foundations, which informed the reconstruction visible in the public park today.
properties.locationAccuracy: Marker beside the reconstructed fort in Fort Zumwalt Park; present logs are a reconstruction, not the original wartime building.
